heading: Scaling exponents and optimal compute allocation depend on setup and fitting choices
definition: the fitted exponents and the compute-optimal split depend on setup and fitting choices (parameter counting, training schedule, data, fitting method), so published laws disagree, and curves can bend away from a single power law.
summary: Several independent groups reproduce changes in fitted exponents and the optimal split of compute between model size and training data with parameter counting, training schedules, data and fitting methods. Curves can depart from a single power law; sensitivity of this split remains unresolved at 10–100B parameters, and controlled evidence above 100B is lacking.

suggested_status.by_scale: R2 in toy models, <1B and 1–10B; R2 at 10–100B for fitted fine-tuning exponents, with allocation sensitivity unresolved; ? above 100B for controlled fit or allocation sensitivity.
suggested_status.reason: Independent studies reproduce conditional sensitivity. Tiny Books-trained models change the optimal-size exponent from 0.49 under total counting to 0.74 under non-embedding counting; synthetic analyses show locally power-law allocation relations (arXiv:2406.12907#R1, #R2, #R5, #R6). Gemstones, spanning 50M–2B, gives 0.4579 with Approach 1 versus 0.6965 with Approach 3 (arXiv:2502.06857#r7, #r9). Qwen3 0.6B–32B FullFT support-data fits change α from 0.51 to 0.33 under oracle-learning-rate refitting, with broad bootstrap intervals (arXiv:2609.01244#R7). Above 100B, the BLOOM-176B result fits existing training logs rather than comparing matched interventions (arXiv:2408.11029#R11). Coverage is recorded in counts: versions.V7.studies_by_size and versions.V7.coverage_by_operation.scaling.by_size. The supporting examples have no author-sharing flag; counts: versions.V7.tested_sharing_an_author_with_an_original identifies overlap elsewhere and does not establish independence for every study.
suggested_status.open_questions: Matched sensitivity experiments above 100B would establish whether the lower-scale allocation findings extend there. Prospective training comparisons between competing fitted allocation prescriptions would distinguish prescription instability from differences in realized optima. A joint controlled attribution of the original published disagreement remains unresolved.

source.title: Training Compute-Optimal Large Language Models
source.authors: Jordan Hoffmann; Sebastian Borgeaud; Arthur Mensch; Elena Buchatskaya; Trevor Cai; Eliza Rutherford; D. de Las Casas; Lisa Anne Hendricks; Johannes Welbl; Aidan Clark; T. Hennigan; Eric Noland; Katie Millican; George van den Driessche; Bogdan Damoc; Aurelia Guy; Simon Osindero; K. Simonyan; Erich Elsen; Jack W. Rae; O. Vinyals; L. Sifre

original_result.setup: Hoffmann et al. compared three fitting methods using over 400 language models trained on MassiveText.
original_result.result: The compute-optimal exponents for model size and training tokens were, respectively, 0.50 and 0.50 with one fitting method; 0.49 and 0.51 with another; and 0.46 and 0.54 with the third. Curvature in the relationship between compute and the lowest achievable loss also changed estimates of optimal model size across fitting ranges.
original_result.interpretation: This is the displayed original-result block, not a guarantee that the original tested every part of this claim.

counting_note: Each group counts distinct sources for this claim. The same source can appear in more than one group or claim; counts are not votes.

untested.what: A joint attribution of the original Kaplan–Hoffmann disagreement that separately controls data, tokenization, counting, training recipe and numerical fitting on matched runs.
untested.basis: arXiv:2406.19146 tests accounting, warmup, decay and tuning on OpenLM, so a blanket claim that reconciliation interventions are missing would be incorrect. Its header says it does not reproduce Kaplan's full setup. arXiv:2404.10102 leaves counting, schedules and data quality untested; arXiv:2509.23963 leaves schedule, data and fitting-method effects untested; arXiv:2502.18969 does not control data source or schedule. counts: versions.V7.coverage_by_operation.scaling.by_family and versions.V7.studies_by_stage describe coverage, not this joint design.

untested.what: Controlled allocation-sensitivity experiments above 100B parameters that hold architecture, context and data matched while varying counting, schedule or fitting choices.
untested.basis: counts: versions.V7.studies_by_size and versions.V7.coverage_by_operation.scaling.by_size include >100B coverage, so large-model evidence is present. However, arXiv:2408.11029#R11 fits an existing BLOOM-176B trajectory, and arXiv:2410.11840#R3–R5 predict OPT-175B loss rather than compare allocation sweeps. OpenLM's problems line limits its grid to 901M; Farseer's validation reaches 25.1B. No supplied part establishes the stronger matched allocation intervention.

untested.what: Prospective selection between the specific competing allocation prescriptions and distant extrapolations produced by alternative fits.
untested.basis: arXiv:2610.34514#r3 gives an extrapolated prediction envelope, not fresh-run validation. arXiv:2607.01487#r5 and arXiv:2608.07222#r47–r48 compare allocations implied by fitted forms. arXiv:2510.18900#r5–r6 compare penalized and unpenalized development-data fits. Held-out loss evaluations elsewhere do not establish which of these allocation prescriptions realizes the minimum. counts: versions.V7.coverage_by_operation.scaling.by_state does not distinguish inferred optima from prospective allocation tests.

untested.what: Whether Neurograf's highest-compute allocation bend persists under independently repeated runs with terminal learning-rate decay.
untested.basis: arXiv:2610.13134#R6–R7 and its method-sensitivity/problems lines describe checkpoint-interpolated optima, intermediate checkpoints without terminal decay and one run per size. No other part supplies this validation for Neurograf. counts: versions.V7.tested_with_uncertainty records uncertainty coverage without establishing independent training repeats for this result.

untested.what: An isolated natural-language test that attributes allocation-exponent changes specifically to gzip-compressibility.
untested.basis: arXiv:2405.16684#R1–R7 tests small synthetic PCFG datasets, including a fixed-vocabulary comparison, and its problems line limits the experiments to synthetic grammars and final training losses. arXiv:2401.02954#r5–r10 changes natural-language corpora without isolating compressibility. Other parts vary distributions or mixtures but do not supply this matched test. counts: versions.V7.coverage_by_operation.scaling.by_family does not identify controlled compressibility interventions.

untested.what: Independent-seed validation of Spectra's offset-induced exponent change.
untested.basis: The verdict fixes for arXiv:2407.12327#r1–r4 state that fit uncertainty is unreported. The checker confirms that no independent training-seed validation of this exponent comparison is reported. No other part supplies repeated training for this particular comparison. counts: versions.V7.tested_with_uncertainty is study-level coverage and cannot establish these missing repeats.

wording_issues.phrase: depend on setup and fitting choices
wording_issues.issue: Dependence is conditional on the intervention and regime. Ordinary Chinchilla counting definitions leave fitted parameters statistically indistinguishable. Protein IsoFLOP, combined-form and IsoLoss fits give similar allocation trends. Qwen fine-tuning exponents barely change between nonlinear least squares and Huber fitting. Enoki optimizer changes mainly shift curve levels while largely preserving exponents. These findings limit any reading that every listed choice materially changes the law.

wording_issues.phrase: the fitted exponents and the compute-optimal split
wording_issues.issue: Loss exponents, allocation exponents and allocation ratios need not change together. Speech tokenization changes loss exponents while preserving approximately equal parameter/token growth. NetHack fitting methods disagree for return optimization but agree within reported intervals for loss optimization. Force-field architectures have different loss exponents while retaining approximately equal parameter/data allocation. Medical-event modeling reports a different optimal token/parameter ratio without requiring different allocation exponents.

Some evidence measures prediction error, ranking quality or a different response variable. DataDecide evaluates downstream-accuracy prediction; LiteTransformerSearch evaluates parameter/perplexity rank correlation; domain-aware HumanEval fits concern downstream task loss; pass-at-k fits concern negative-log sampling success. These results cannot be pooled as estimates of a held-out pretraining-loss exponent, and changes in fit quality alone do not establish changed exponents.

The allocation variable and constraint need specification. The dense/MoE study uses FLOPs per token as model scale; encoder MLM uses FLOPs per token including attention. ViT results allocate compute among width, depth and MLP dimensions. Sparse-MoE total and active parameter optima move in opposite directions at a fixed budget. These quantities are distinct from parameter/token allocation exponents across compute budgets.

An optimum inferred from a fitted surface requires qualification. MIST's competing allocations come from penalized versus unpenalized fits; DIVER's allocations are predictions from fitted laws; chess allocations are analytic consequences of fitted exponents. Ambiguous Fits reports a distant prediction envelope without validating its extremes through training. These establish prescription sensitivity rather than independently measured superiority of each prescription.

Controlled sensitivity establishes possible causes of disagreement, with some direct reconciliation evidence. OpenLM changes accounting, warmup, decay and tuning within its experiments; (Mis)Fitting changes forms and fitting choices on shared observations; the Chinchilla replication tests numerical fitting. These do not jointly isolate every difference between the original published experiments. The supervised-distillation paper's primary-driver counting explanation is cited rather than established by its own controlled comparison.

wording_issues.phrase: curves can bend away from a single power law
wording_issues.issue: Saturation or raw-loss curvature need not reject a power law for excess loss above a floor. The RoPE ladder favors a saturating power law over an additional hinge break. Pythia's estimated exponent changes with offset inclusion; subtracting estimated optimal loss improves EDM2 envelope linearity. Spectra's same-run exponent also changes between offset and plain forms. Floor specification and an additional change of scaling regime are distinct tests.

wording_issues.phrase: curves can bend away from a single power law
wording_issues.issue: The curve and resource constraint must accompany a bending claim. Relational Transformer U-shapes occur when one data axis grows with the other fixed; EHR U-shapes occur under finite-data repeated training. Sparse-model slope changes follow individual trajectories. The synthetic-rewrite curvature correction concerns an off-frontier loss surface and leaves its compute frontier unchanged. These observations do not all demonstrate bending of an unconstrained compute-optimal frontier.

Coefficient variation can reflect weak identification rather than a well-determined change in a physical or asymptotic exponent. PCFG fits include negative and degenerate asymptotes. Synthetic market-model exponents are explicitly described as poorly identified. Polish same-checkpoint fits are exactly determined by their sparse ladder and change with evaluation protocol. Ambiguous Fits finds substantially different extrapolations among fits with equally good or better objectives.

Some comparisons change several factors together and cannot isolate the named cause. The French/English comparison changes language, corpus, codebase and hardware. The C4/mixed-data comparison also changes context, batch size and evaluation distribution; experiment-specific tokenizer differences are not reported. The standard-parameterization versus µP comparison changes context and batch size. HGT changes the training objective and fitted metric together. Such results establish conditional differences without assigning them uniquely to data, parameterization or objective.

method_sensitivity.factor: Fitting objective, initialization and residual space
method_sensitivity.what: For Transformer Token/Param models of 162M–6863M parameters, α ranges over 0.53–0.64 with Huber δ in γ-modified xLSTM-study fits. QAT law fitting is initialization-sensitive, and MSE generalizes worse than Huber. Farseer's standard-regression errors are about ten times its piecewise-fitting errors. OPF AC-MU data exponents are −0.487 under log-space OLS and −0.328 under nonlinear least squares, showing observed fitting dependence despite a non-monotone MAE series. Other OPF series in r1, r3 and r7 show near-invariant exponents, narrowly challenging fitting dependence under that intervention; r8 retains a smaller effect, −0.611 versus −0.557.

method_sensitivity.factor: Experiment acquisition, law selection and compute accounting
method_sensitivity.what: In ScAn-Bench, estimated compute-optimal model size N* depends on law family and acquisition strategy. For OpenCLIP, empirical-power-law N* prediction succeeds while Chinchilla3 allocation prediction fails under invalid 6ND compute accounting. Localized acquisition can poorly estimate N*. CARBS with Chinchilla3 has the lowest final N* regret among compared acquisitions; comparison with the empirical-power-law result shows dependence on the fitted law. These results concern allocation estimation and do not establish failure of the underlying allocation law.

method_sensitivity.factor: Evaluation metric, protocol and optimization target
method_sensitivity.what: NetHack BC return-optimal parameter/sample exponents are 0.51/0.49 with IsoFLOP fitting versus 0.605/0.395 parametrically, while loss-optimal fits agree within intervals. The same Polish checkpoints give α=0.202 under dense evaluation and 0.355 under a twenty-window probe; both fits are exactly determined from three points. TESSERA encoder allocation exponents are 0.36 under downstream-score selection and 0.02 under normalized-loss selection. Pythia's negative-log pass-at-k compute exponent increases approximately 0.12→0.375 with k on GSM8K and reaches approximately 0.58 on MATH.

method_sensitivity.factor: Token compression, data-volume units and compute axis
method_sensitivity.what: English subword-tokenization sweeps at 1×10^19–2×10^21 FLOPs find approximately constant optimal bytes/parameter while tokens/parameter change with compression. qLSTM's normalized-perplexity slope is −0.112 against accelerator time versus −0.134 against FLOPs. Its fitted best configurations are mini (27.8M parameters) at 6 h, tiny (55.9M) at 12 h, and small (117.3M) at 24, 48 and 96 h. Raw versus unigram-compressed speech gives loss α/β=0.25/0.24 versus 0.15/0.16 while retaining approximately equal allocation. Synthetic graph-motif fits have R²=0.84 using graph count and 0.94 using node or edge count. These comparisons change measurement units or representation, with task-specific interpretations.

method_sensitivity.factor: Learning-rate tuning, schedules and hyperparameter transfer
method_sensitivity.what: Per-scale encoder tuning changes SQuAD 1.1 slope from −0.30 to −0.22 and R² from 0.830 to 0.998; other tasks show little exponent change. DataComp cosine-to-constant schedules change openCLIP ImageNet-error exponent from −0.227 to −0.168 and openMaMMUT from −0.233 to −0.379. Llama-style Muon width fits change from 0.50 to 0.60 with transferred learning rate; Adam remains 0.52.

method_sensitivity.factor: Repetition calibration, regularization and experimental constraints
method_sensitivity.what: Refitting the C4 single-epoch baseline changes R² from 0.711 to 0.989 and reverses an allocation recommendation. On a shared DCLM grid, law choice changes inferred MIR efficiency at 400M unique tokens over 1.29×–1.84×. In Equation 21 fits with η=0, adding 520M runs changes repetition exponent q from 1.309 to 0.747 on PubMed and 1.175 to 0.864 on Caselaw. In repeated-data text sweeps, optimal repetitions decrease with model size at fixed unique data but remain approximately flat at fixed unique-data/parameter ratio; embedding counting also changes the fitted size term.

TriLM/FloatLM joint fits give α/β=0.32/0.81 versus 0.56/0.53, with different size ranges and flagged FloatLM units. Equal-sparsity MoEs with 128/top-8 versus 256/top-16 experts give 0.28/0.16 versus 0.64/0.36. Neural force-field FLOPs exponents range from 0.14 for unconstrained MPNN to 0.40 for eSEN while allocation stays approximately 0.5/0.5. Rigid-body baseline/equivariant transformers give allocation exponents 0.294/0.706 versus 0.678/0.322; their FLOP constants also differ.

method_sensitivity.factor: Task spectra, schedule boundaries and conditional theory
method_sensitivity.what: Projected-SGD feature-learning theory changes hard-task time scaling from t^−β to t^(−2β/(1+β)); easy-task asymptotic exponents remain unchanged. Random-feature theory gives time exponent (a−1)/(a+b−1) under constant or power-law learning rates versus (a−1)/max(a,b) under optimal schedules. Softmax teacher–student theory becomes logarithmic at inverse-time learning-rate decay and has nonzero limiting loss/error for faster decay. In noisy quadratic-network theory (Δ>0, ℓ<α/2−1), overfitting rise E=Θ(d^{ρ−α+1}) requires (α−1)/(2γ)<ρ<min(1,α−1) and α<1+2γ. Further decay E=Θ(d^{α−ρ−1}) requires 1<α<2 and α−1<ρ<ρeff,1(α,γ). Width decay and plateau occur in other stated regimes. These are conditional theoretical results.

method_sensitivity.factor: Allocation estimator, functional form and prescription validation
method_sensitivity.what: Digitized Llama 3 IsoFLOP data imply 16.1T optimal tokens under Approach 2 versus 10.1T under Approach 3 at 3.8×10^25 FLOPs; perfectly centered, symmetric noise-free synthetic surfaces recover the true allocation exactly. Additive and coupled Farseer fits imply opposite-sign token/parameter allocation trends. Shared-grid BERT retrieval fits imply an interior optimum under an additive law and none under a multiplicative law. Visual diffusion post-training gives optimal-size a=0.7021 parametrically, 0.5492 with an envelope and 0.4538 with IsoFLOP fitting. Derived prescriptions need independent training validation.

method_sensitivity.factor: Conditional robustness: explicit challenges to fitting/counting dependence
method_sensitivity.what: Ordinary reported, standard-formula and best-fit-formula Chinchilla parameter counts leave fitted parameters statistically unchanged and optimal tokens/parameter around 20. Synthetic additive offsets of approximately −4.0e7 to −4.0e6 lower the fitted parameter exponent and make the optimal ratio decrease with compute; offsets of 4.0e6 to 4.0e7 raise the exponent relative to baseline and make the ratio increase. Protein CLM/MLM combined Chinchilla-form and IsoLoss fits give trends similar to IsoFLOP fits, despite objective-dependent allocations. On the EvoLM Qwen fine-tuning grid, nonlinear least squares and Huber give identical or nearly identical exponents: QLoRA-1.5B λ=0.26 under both. Robustness applies to the stated ordinary counting or fitting intervention; synthetic offsets show observed dependence.
